title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON MAINTAINING SHIPPING AND PORT FUNCTIONS IN PREPARATION FOR EMERGENCY SITUATIONS, ETC.
title_original: 비상사태등에 대비하기 위한 해운 및 항만 기능 유지에 관한 법률 시행령
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON MAINTAINING SHIPPING AND PORT FUNCTIONS IN PREPARATION FOR EMERGENCY SITUATIONS, ETC.

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on Maintaining Shipping and Port Functions in Preparation for Emergency Situations, etc. and matters necessary for the enforcement thereof.

Article 2 (Definitions)
"Cases where serious impediments prescribed by Presidential Decree occur" in subparagraph 1 (c) of Article 2 of the Act on Maintaining Shipping and Port Functions in Preparation for Emergency Situations, etc. (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means the following cases:
1. Where it is difficult to maintain shipping and port functions due to a disaster under subparagraph 1 of Article 3 of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety;
2. Where the smooth transportation of passengers or cargo is impeded due to the bankruptcy, etc. of a person licensed to engage in marine passenger transportation business under Article 4 (1) of the Marine Transportation Act or a person registered to engage in coastal cargo transportation business or overseas cargo transportation business under Article 24 (1) or (2) of that Act, or where it is difficult to maintain the functions of harbor transportation under Article 2 (1) of the Harbor Transport Business Act due to suspension of business, etc. by a person registered to engage in harbor transportation business under Article 4 (1) of that Act or a person who has registered or reported a harbor transportation-related business under Article 26-3 (1) of that Act.

Article 3 (Matters to Be Included in Master Plans for Maintaining Shipping and Port Functions)
"Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 4 (2) 4 of the Act means the following matters: <Amended on Jun. 25, 2024>
1. Matters concerning criteria for designation, change of designation, and release from designation of national essential ships;
2. Matters concerning improvement of the national essential ship and port operation agreement systems;
2-2. Matters concerning designation and operation of national essential pilots and improvement of the relevant system;
3. Other matters concerning maintenance of shipping and port functions in preparation for emergency situations, etc. that the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries deems necessary.

Article 4 (Public Notice of Master Plans for Maintaining Shipping and Port Functions, etc.)
When intending to publicly notify a master plan for maintaining shipping and port functions in preparation for emergency situations, etc. under Article 4 (1) of the Act or an annual implementation plan under paragraph (5) of that Article (hereinafter referred to as an "implementation plan") pursuant to paragraph (4) or (7) of that Article, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall do so by publishing it in the Official Gazette or posting it on the website of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 5 (Formulation and Implementation of Implementation Plans, etc.)
(1) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall formulate an implementation plan for the following year by December 31 each year pursuant to Article 4 (5) of the Act.
(2) An implementation plan shall include the following matters: <Amended on Jun. 25, 2024>
1. Results and evaluation of the preceding year's implementation plan;
2. Direction for implementation of projects in the relevant year;
3. Detailed project plans, including project details and required budgets for the relevant year;
4. Other matters necessary to carry out designation of national essential ships, conclusion of port operation agreements, designation of national essential pilots, etc.

Article 6 (Amendment of Master Plans for Maintaining Shipping and Port Functions)
"Cases of changing minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso of Article 4 (8) of the Act means any of the following cases:
1. Where terminology is changed due to amendment of other statutes, plans, guidelines, etc.;
2. Where part of a plan is supplemented, such as by correcting statistics on future cargo volume, etc. or simple wording.

Article 7 (Criteria for Designation of National Essential Ships, etc.)
(1) "Ships meeting the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the former part of Article 5 (1) of the Act, with the exception of its subparagraphs, means ships meeting all of the following criteria:
1. A ship with an international gross tonnage of at least 10,000 tons under Article 3 (1) 1 of the Ship Act and less than 20 years of age; provided, the ship-age criterion shall not apply to ships falling under the proviso of Article 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the International Ship Registration Act;
2. A ship transporting materials that have a significant impact on the national economy or national security, such as military supplies, grain, crude oil, liquefied gas, coal, or raw materials for iron manufacturing.
(2) When designating national essential ships pursuant to Article 5 (1) of the Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may give priority to designation of ships for which multi-year transportation contracts have been concluded with shippers having the nationality of the Republic of Korea.
(3) National essential ships shall be designated for one fiscal year of the Government at a time, and, unless there are special circumstances, ships designated as national essential ships shall be given priority for designation as national essential ships in the following fiscal year.

Article 8 (Procedures for Designation of National Essential Ships, etc.)
(1) When intending to designate national essential ships pursuant to Article 5 (1) of the Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall finalize the plan for designation of national essential ships for the following year by December 5 and publish that fact in the Official Gazette or post it on the website of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
(2) The owner of a ship who intends to have the ship designated as a national essential ship under Article 5 (1) of the Act, a person licensed to engage in regular overseas passenger transportation business or irregular overseas passenger transportation business under Article 4 (1) of the Marine Transportation Act, a person registered to engage in overseas cargo transportation business under Article 24 (2) of that Act, or a person registered to engage in ship leasing business under Article 33 (1) of that Act shall apply to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries for designation as a national essential ship, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
(3) Upon receipt of an application for designation as a national essential ship under paragraph (2), the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall examine whether the designation criteria are met, designate the relevant ship as a national essential ship by December 31, and notify the applicant of the designation without delay.
(4) Where examination of technical matters is necessary when finalizing a plan for designation of national essential ships under paragraph (1) or designating national essential ships under paragraph (3), the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may request the Korea Ocean Business Corporation under the Korea Ocean Business Corporation Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Korea Ocean Business Corporation") to examine those matters and submit its opinion.

Article 9 (Restrictions on Foreign Seafarers Serving Aboard Ships)
(1) The limit on foreign seafarers serving aboard national essential ships under Article 5 (6) of the Act shall be the number obtained by subtracting the number under subparagraph 2 from the number under subparagraph 1: <Amended on May 7, 2024>
1. The maximum number of seafarers among the maximum number of persons permitted aboard the national essential ship under Article 8 (2) and (3) of the Ship Safety Act;
2. The number of seafarers who are nationals of the Republic of Korea necessary for safe navigation of the national essential ship, as determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
(2) When designating a national essential ship pursuant to Article 8, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may order restrictions on service aboard the national essential ship by foreign seafarers exceeding the limit under paragraph (1). In such cases, the person who has obtained designation as a national essential ship shall take measures to bring the number of foreign seafarers into conformity with the limit under paragraph (1) within six months from the date of the order restricting foreign seafarers' service aboard the ship and shall notify the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries of that fact without delay.
(3) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), where special circumstances arise, such as repair of a ship, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may temporarily relax the limit on foreign seafarers serving aboard the ship or refrain from applying it.
(4) Procedures for relaxing or excluding application of the limit on foreign seafarers serving aboard ships pursuant to paragraph (3) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 10 (Matters on Which Opinions Are to Be Heard, etc.)
(1) "Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the role of national essential ships in emergency situations, etc." in Article 6 of the Act means the following matters:
1. Matters concerning the number of ships, by use, eligible for designation as national essential ships and methods for calculating compensation for loss, etc.;
2. Matters concerning the number of foreign seafarers who may serve aboard national essential ships;
3. Matters concerning the role of national essential ships when emergency situations, etc. occur;
4. Matters concerning development of the abilities of seafarers serving aboard national essential ships and support therefor;
5. Matters concerning improvement of the national essential ship designation system;
6. Other matters deemed necessary by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries for efficient designation and stable maintenance of national essential ships.
(2) "Relevant organizations prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 6 of the Act means the following organizations: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
1. Federations of seafarers' labor unions under Article 5 (2) of the International Ship Registration Act;
2. Associations of overseas transportation business operators under Article 5 (2) of the International Ship Registration Act;
3. The Korea International Trade Association established with permission from the Minister of Trade and Industry pursuant to Article 32 of the Civil Act;
4. Other specialized institutions in the field of shipping logistics determined by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 11 (Support for National Essential Ships and Enterprises That Have Concluded Agreements)
(1) Port facility usage fees that may be fully or partially exempted under Article 9 of the Act shall be ship dues under Article 46 (1) 1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Harbor Act and Article 13 (1) 1 (a) of the Enforcement Decree of the Port Authority Act. <Amended on Jul. 28, 2020>
(2) Port facility usage fees that may be fully or partially exempted under Article 12 of the Act shall be ship dues and fees for exclusive use of port facilities under Article 46 (1) 1 and 4 of the Enforcement Decree of the Harbor Act, ship dues and exclusive-use fees under Article 13 (1) 1 (a) and (d) of the Enforcement Decree of the Port Authority Act, and rents under subparagraph 2 of that paragraph. <Amended on Jul. 28, 2020>
(3) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall determine matters necessary for support for national essential ships and enterprises that have concluded agreements, other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) and (2).

Article 12 (Qualification Criteria for Business Operators Eligible to Conclude Port Operation Agreements, etc.)
(1) "Qualifications prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 10 (1) of the Act means the qualifications specified in attached Table 1.
(2) A port operation agreement may be concluded for a period not exceeding three years.

Article 13 (Procedures for Concluding Port Operation Agreements)
(1) A person who intends to conclude a port operation agreement shall submit an application for a port operation agreement and the documents prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries by January 31.
(2) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall evaluate the particulars entered in the application and documents submitted under paragraph (1), select persons with whom to conclude port operation agreements, and conclude port operation agreements by port and by field by the end of February.
(3) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall issue a certificate of conclusion of a port operation agreement, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, to a person who has concluded a port operation agreement under Article 10 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "agreement enterprise").
(4) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall determine matters necessary for the procedures for concluding agreements, such as methods for evaluating applicants for port operation agreements, other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (3).

Article 14 (Scale of Port Operation Agreements)
(1) The number of persons with whom the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries concludes port operation agreements under Article 10 (1) of the Act shall not exceed one-tenth of the number of domestic business operators in each category of business operator specified in attached Table 1.
(2) Where the Korea Marine Environment Corporation under Article 96 of the Marine Environment Management Act is eligible to conclude a port operation agreement as a business operator under subparagraph 1 of attached Table 1, it shall be excluded when calculating the ratio under paragraph (1).
(3) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), where the supply of port facilities is expanded due to amendment of a master plan for ports formulated under Article 5 of the Harbor Act, port operation agreements may be operated beyond the limit under paragraph (1).

Article 14-2 (Designation and Operation of National Essential Pilots, etc.)
(1) A pilot who intends to be designated as a national essential pilot under Article 12-2 (1) of the Act shall meet all of the following qualification criteria:
1. The pilot shall be a Grade I pilot of the relevant pilotage district;
2. The pilot shall not have been subject to a disposition revoking the pilot's license under Article 9 (1) of the Pilotage Act during the preceding three years;
3. The aggregate period of business suspensions imposed under Article 9 (1) of the Pilotage Act during the preceding three years shall be less than 90 days.
(2) A pilot who intends to be designated as a national essential pilot under Article 12-2 (1) of the Act shall apply to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
(3) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall decide whether to grant designation, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, and notify the applicant of the result within 30 days from the date of receipt of an application for designation under paragraph (2).
(4) When designating national essential pilots pursuant to Article 12-2 (1) of the Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall designate national essential pilots in a number ranging from at least 10 percent to not more than 30 percent of the number of pilots in each pilotage district (any fractional number shall be rounded up to the next whole person); provided, where the number of national essential pilots calculated under the main clause is less than two, two shall be designated.
(5) Matters necessary for designation and operation of national essential pilots, etc., other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (4), shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 15 (Standards for Compensation for Loss Caused by Compliance with Orders)
(1) The standards for the amount of compensation for loss under Article 13 (1) 1, 3, and 4 of the Act shall be as follows, according to the type of loss: <Amended on Jun. 25, 2024>
1. Loss caused by destruction of or damage to property: The standards specified in the following items:
(a) Where damaged property can be repaired: An amount equivalent to the repair cost shall be compensated;
(b) Where property is destroyed or damaged property cannot be repaired: The exchange value of the relevant property at the time of the loss shall be compensated;
2. Property loss other than loss caused by destruction of or damage to property: Compensation shall be provided to the extent that there is a proximate causal relationship with compliance with a mobilization and transportation order under Article 5 (3) of the Act, an order to engage in work under Article 10 (2) of the Act, or an order to engage in work under Article 12-2 (2) of the Act;
3. Death or injury: In the case of death, the amount determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Health and Welfare pursuant to Article 12 (1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons Who Died or Were Injured for the Public Good shall be compensated; and in the case of injury, the amount under Article 12 (2) of that Decree shall be compensated according to the grades under Article 2 and attached Table 1 of that Decree.
(2) Article 10 of the Act on Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons Who Died or Were Injured for the Public Good shall apply mutatis mutandis to the order of priority for payment of compensation for loss under paragraph (1) 3.

Article 16 (Standards for Compensation for Loss Due to Restrictions on Foreign Seafarers Serving Aboard Ships)
(1) Compensation for loss under Article 13 (1) 2 of the Act shall be calculated according to the following formula:

Compensation for loss = (A - B) × (C - D)
A: Number of foreign seafarers under the standards for service aboard ships by foreign seafarers under Article 5 (2) of the International Ship Registration Act.
B: Limit on the number of foreign seafarers serving aboard international essential ships under Article 9 (1).
C: Average annual wages of Korean seafarers serving aboard national essential ships.
D: Average annual wages of foreign seafarers serving aboard international ships.

(2) The following matters shall be considered when calculating compensation for loss under paragraph (1):
1. The calculation shall be made separately by occupational category and rank of officers and ratings under subparagraphs 5 and 6 of Article 2 of the Seafarers Act and by the use of ships registered under Article 8 (1) of the Ship Act;
2. Where a national essential ship operates for at least 320 days a year, the full annual compensation amount shall be paid; and where it operates for less than 320 days, compensation shall be paid in proportion to the actual number of operating days on the basis of 320 days.
(3) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall publicly notify the compensation for loss calculated under paragraph (1) by December 31.
(4) Where the limit on foreign seafarers serving aboard ships under Article 9 (1) is violated, the compensation for loss under Article 13 (1) 2 of the Act shall be paid after reducing part or all of it in accordance with attached Table 2.

Article 17 (Procedures and Methods for Compensation for Loss)
(1) A person who intends to receive compensation for loss under Article 13 (1) of the Act shall submit a claim for payment of compensation for loss and the documents prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
(2) Upon receipt of a claim under paragraph (1), the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may, where necessary to calculate compensation for loss, require the person claiming compensation to submit supporting or supplementary materials, and may have specialized institutions or experts in the relevant field appraise, evaluate, or investigate the items of loss.
(3) In the case of a loss under Article 13 (1) 1, 3, or 4 of the Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall, unless there are special grounds, decide whether to pay compensation for loss and the amount of compensation within 60 days from the date of receipt of the claim for payment of compensation for loss. <Amended on Jun. 25, 2024>
(4) Where a claim for payment of compensation for a loss under Article 13 (1) 1, 3, or 4 of the Act falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall decide to dismiss the claim: <Amended on Jun. 25, 2024>
1. Where the claimant has filed a claim for payment of compensation for loss on the same grounds and has received a decision on whether compensation for loss is to be paid; provided, this shall not apply where a claimant who has received a decision not to pay compensation for loss makes a prima facie showing that new evidence capable of proving the loss has been discovered;
2. Where the claim for payment of compensation for loss fails to meet the requirements and procedures; provided, this shall not apply where the defects can be corrected.
(5) In the case of a loss under Article 13 (1) 1, 3, or 4 of the Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall notify the claimant of the particulars specified in the following subparagraphs within 10 days from the date of the decision under paragraphs (3) and (4) of this Article and, where the Minister has decided to pay compensation for loss, shall pay the compensation within 30 days from the date of notification, unless there are special grounds: <Amended on Jun. 25, 2024>
1. Where a decision has been made to pay compensation for loss: Grounds for compensation, amount of compensation, and method of compensation;
2. Where a claim for payment of compensation for loss has been dismissed or a decision has been made not to pay compensation for loss: Reasons for the decision.
(6) In the case of a loss under Article 13 (1) 2 of the Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall pay the claimant the compensation for loss calculated under Article 16 of this Decree without delay.
(7) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall pay compensation for loss by depositing it into a deposit account designated by the person entitled to receive compensation for loss [referring to an account at a postal service agency under the Postal Savings and Insurance Act (hereinafter referred to as a "postal service agency") or a bank under the Banking Act (hereinafter referred to as a "bank")]; provided, where there are unavoidable grounds, such as the person entitled to receive compensation residing in an area without a postal service agency or bank, the compensation may be paid in cash upon the request of that person.
(8) Compensation for loss shall be paid in a lump sum; provided, where special circumstances, such as a budget shortfall, prevent payment in a lump sum, it may be paid in installments with the consent of the claimant.
(9) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall determine matters necessary for claiming and paying compensation for loss, other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (8).

Article 18 (Recovery of Compensation for Loss)
(1) When intending to recover compensation for loss pursuant to Article 14 (1) of the Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall, without delay, send a written notice specifying the following matters to the person from whom the compensation is to be recovered:
1. Grounds for recovery;
2. Amount to be recovered;
3. Payment deadline;
4. Institution to which payment is to be made;
5. Whether payment in installments is available and how to apply for payment in installments.
(2) The payment deadline under paragraph (1) 3 shall be at least 30 days after the date of written notification under that paragraph.
(3) Where a person who has received notice under paragraph (1) fails to pay the compensation for loss to be recovered by the payment deadline, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall, without delay, issue a written demand for payment of the amount to be recovered, specifying a further period of at least 30 days.
(4) Where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries recovers compensation for loss on the grounds specified in Article 14 (1) 2 of the Act, the Minister may allow payment in installments over a period not exceeding one year. In such cases, the number of installments shall not exceed four, and each installment shall be the amount obtained by dividing the total compensation for loss to be recovered by the number of installments.
(5) A person who intends to pay compensation for loss to be recovered in installments under paragraph (4) shall apply to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries for payment in installments by the payment deadline under paragraph (1) 3 or the payment deadline specified in the demand for payment under paragraph (3).

Article 19 (Delegation and Entrustment of Authority, etc.)
(1) Pursuant to Article 16 (1) of the Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall delegate the following authority in State-managed trade ports under Article 3 (2) 1 of the Harbor Act to the heads of the competent regional offices of oceans and fisheries, and shall delegate the following authority in locally managed trade ports under subparagraph 2 of that paragraph to the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayors, Do Governors, and the Special Self-Governing Province Governor: <Amended on Jun. 25, 2024>
1. Conclusion of port operation agreements under Article 10 (1) of the Act;
2. Orders to agreement enterprises to engage in work under Article 10 (2) of the Act;
3. Termination of port operation agreements under Article 11 of the Act;
3-2. Designation of national essential pilots under Article 12-2 (1) of the Act, orders to national essential pilots to engage in work under paragraph (2) of that Article, and revocation of designation of national essential pilots under paragraph (5) of that Article;
4. Compensation for loss under Article 13 (1) 3 and 4 of the Act;
5. Recovery of compensation for loss under Article 14 of the Act (limited to recovery of compensation for loss under subparagraph 4);
6. Requests for submission of data under Article 15 (1) 2 of the Act;
7. Imposition of administrative fines under Article 19 (1) 2 of the Act on persons who fail to comply with a request for submission of data under Article 15 (1) 2 of the Act;
8. Issuance of certificates of conclusion of port operation agreements under Article 13 (3).
(2) Pursuant to Article 16 (2) of the Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall entrust the following affairs to the Korea Ocean Business Corporation:
1. Hearing of opinions under Article 6 of the Act;
2. Conduct of education or training under Article 7 of the Act;
3. Compensation for loss under Article 13 (1) 2 of the Act.

Article 20 (Standards for Imposition of Administrative Fines)
The standards for imposition of administrative fines under Article 19 (1) of the Act shall be as specified in attached Table 3.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 30341, Jan. 7, 2020>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on January 16, 2020.

Article 2 (Amendment of Other Statutes)
The Enforcement Decree of the International Ship Registration Act is partially amended as follows:
Articles 3 through 8, Article 8-2, and Article 9 shall each be deleted.
Subparagraphs 2 and 3 of Article 10 shall each be deleted.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 30876, Jul. 28, 2020>
(Enforcement Decree of the Harbor Act)

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on July 30, 2020.

Articles 2 through 13 Omitted.

Article 14 (Amendment of Other Statutes)
(1) through (7) Omitted.
(8) The Enforcement Decree of the Act on Maintaining Shipping and Port Functions in Preparation for Emergency Situations, etc. is partially amended as follows:
In Article 11 (1), "Article 28 (1) 1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Harbor Act" shall be amended to "Article 46 (1) 1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Harbor Act"; and in paragraph (2) of that Article, "Article 28 (1) 1 and 4 of the Enforcement Decree of the Harbor Act" shall be amended to "Article 46 (1) 1 and 4 of the Enforcement Decree of the Harbor Act."
(9) through (31) Omitted.

Article 15 Omitted.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 33434, Apr. 25, 2023>
(Presidential Decree Partially Amending 61 Statutes to Support the Economic Recovery of Micro Enterprises)

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Applicability to Administrative Dispositions, Penalty Surcharges, or Administrative Fines)
The amended provisions of Articles 1 through 61 shall also apply where an administrative disposition is issued or a penalty surcharge or administrative fine is imposed after this Decree enters into force for a violation committed before this Decree enters into force.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 34500, May 7, 2024>

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 34604, Jun. 25, 2024>

This Decree shall enter into force on June 30, 2024.

(Presidential Decree Partially Amending 306 Statutes to Reflect Government Reorganization)

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation; provided, among the Presidential Decrees amended by this Decree, the amendments to Presidential Decrees promulgated before this Decree enters into force but whose enforcement dates have not yet arrived shall enter into force on the respective enforcement dates of those Presidential Decrees.
